patterns.coaching_expression: Shrink the coast — the car should always be braking, turning, or driving.
patterns.drill: Next session: find where you're on neither pedal mid-corner and close that gap by a fraction — brake a touch later or pick up throttle a touch sooner.
patterns.driving_principle: Neither pedal working means neither axle is doing anything useful — the car coasts through time that braking, turning, or driving could have used.
patterns.strength_expression: Almost no coasting here — the car is braking, turning or driving nearly all the way through.

patterns.coaching_expression: Pick up later but build smoothly; if you have to lift, you opened it too early.
patterns.drill: Next session: delay throttle pickup slightly and apply it as one continuous build to full throttle — no stabs, no lifts.
patterns.driving_principle: A lift after picking up throttle means the pickup point was a guess, not a commitment — the car had to give back grip mid-application it never should have been asked for.
patterns.strength_expression: Your throttle pickup is committed — once you open it, it stays open, so the rear never has to give grip back.

patterns.coaching_expression: Settle the entry, then one committed input to the apex.
patterns.drill: Next session: pick your turn-in point before the corner and commit to a single steering input. Ignore lap time; count your own corrections.
patterns.driving_principle: Every extra steering correction between turn-in and apex is the car negotiating a line you haven't committed to — each one scrubs speed the corner didn't need to lose.
patterns.strength_expression: You're committing to the line — turn-in to apex on one input, with no mid-corner renegotiation.

patterns.coaching_expression: One pedal at a time — hand the car cleanly from brake to throttle.
patterns.drill: Next session: find the exact moment you're fully off the brake before any throttle. Widen that gap if it's currently negative.
patterns.driving_principle: Throttle and brake fighting each other confuses the weight transfer the car needs to plant one axle at a time. Beyond a deliberate heel-toe blip, overlap just burns the front brakes against the rear tires.
patterns.gate_reason: insufficient breadth: 1 track(s) < 2 — seen at one track only, so it may be the track rather than the driver
patterns.strength_expression: Clean handoff — you're off the brake before you're on the throttle, so the car always knows which axle it's working.

patterns.coaching_expression: Match a lap before you try to beat it — repeatability comes before pace.
patterns.drill: Next session: try to execute this corner exactly the same way three laps in a row. Ignore lap time; judge yourself only on how close the three felt.
patterns.driving_principle: A technique that varies lap to lap isn't a technique yet — it's a range of outcomes. Pace built on an inconsistent input is pace you can't reliably reproduce under pressure.
patterns.gate_reason: insufficient breadth: 1 track(s) < 2 — seen at one track only, so it may be the track rather than the driver
patterns.strength_expression: You're repeating yourself — your inputs land in the same place lap after lap, which is what makes pace reproducible.

patterns.coaching_expression: Lap time hides in mid-corner speed, not entry bravery.
patterns.drill: Next session: on this corner, ignore your braking point entirely. Only chase the number on the speedo at the apex.
patterns.driving_principle: Mid-corner speed compounds down the following straight; an entry-braking gain rarely does. A real, repeatable gap between your faster and slower laps through the middle of a corner is where the lap time actually is.
patterns.gate_reason: insufficient breadth: 1 track(s) < 2 — seen at one track only, so it may be the track rather than the driver
patterns.strength_expression: Your mid-corner speed holds up — there's no repeatable gap between your quicker and slower laps through the middle.

strengths.coaching_expression: Let the fronts finish their work before you ask them to steer — trail the brake in, don't drop it.
strengths.drill: Next session: on medium-speed corners, deliberately delay full brake release ~0.2 s into the corner. Ignore lap time. Feel the car keep pointing at the apex.
strengths.driving_principle: Front tires can't both decelerate and steer at the limit. Releasing brake pressure well before turn-in unloads the front axle before it has finished slowing the car, so there's no grip left to rotate.
strengths.gate_reason: insufficient breadth: 1 track(s) < 2 — seen at one track only, so it may be the track rather than the driver
strengths.strength_expression: Your brake release is doing its job — the fronts stay loaded into the corner instead of being dropped at turn-in.

strengths.coaching_expression: This might be about commitment more than outright speed — you're giving up entry speed sooner than the corner needs.
